final_recommendation: The room converged on a protocol amendment with automatic tariff snapback on labor violations, contingent on simultaneous release of Mexico's written commitment and AFL-CIO endorsement by Wednesday. Congress commits to Friday markup and Tuesday floor vote if no amendments are introduced to the labor enforcement language.
minority_objections: Canada repeatedly warned that any protocol renegotiation risks reopening dairy and Chapter 19 concessions
Mexico initially resisted zero-appeal snapback language as sovereignty infringement before ultimately conceding
key_conflicts: Congress vs. Mexico on automatic tariff trigger with no appeal window (sovereignty vs. enforcement)
Labor vs. Business on timing of endorsements and vote certainty
Canada vs. all parties on risk that protocol amendment cracks open settled terms
key_concessions: Mexico accepted binding automatic tariff snapback with zero procedural appeal window
Congress agreed to lock protocol text as-is with no amendments to labor language
Labor agreed to Wednesday endorsement contingent on receiving final text by end of day
Business accepted delayed vote timeline to secure labor sign-off
red_lines: Congress: no vote without AFL-CIO endorsement of snapback language
Labor: withdrawal of endorsement if Congress rewords snapback provisions
Mexico: no acceptance of unilateral U.S. tariff authority without due process
Canada: any protocol renegotiation that touches original USMCA text triggers dairy/Chapter 19 reopening
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation risk: Mexico's labor reforms are 'already law' but actual facility-level compliance remains unverified
Political timing risk: 48-hour window between labor endorsement and markup creates space for defections
Enforcement asymmetry: automatic snapback gives U.S. unilateral power with no reciprocal mechanism for Mexico
Public narrative fragility: deal depends on media framing holding through vote, vulnerable to counter-messaging
downstream_risk_variables: Whether Mexico's written confirmation language exactly matches Congress's interpretation of 'automatic' and 'zero appeal'
Whether AFL-CIO board actually delivers Wednesday endorsement after reviewing final text
Whether Congress vote count holds between Friday markup and Tuesday floor vote
Whether Canada's government accepts protocol amendment as truly separate from original USMCA or demands reopening
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved procedural convergence on a tight timeline (Wednesday text drop, Friday markup, Tuesday vote) but left unresolved: (1) whether Mexico's 'already enacted' labor reforms are actually enforceable at facility level, (2) whether the vote count is solid enough to survive 4-day markup-to-floor window, (3) whether the protocol amendment truly insulates Canada's settled terms from renegotiation pressure, and (4) whether the automatic snapback mechanism is politically sustainable for Mexico's government beyond ratification.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress opened with 'I've got the votes to kill this thing if we vote today' and ratification prospects dropped to 32% before protocol amendment; drove entire room structure
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Labor's demand for automatic snapback with zero appeal dominated R1-R7; union's conditional Wednesday endorsement was the unlock for ratification path
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Business consistently pushed for vote certainty and timeline but accepted delayed markup to secure labor sign-off; supportive but not driving
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Canada raised dairy/Chapter 19 reopening risk in every round but accepted protocol amendment as separate; defensive posture, not driving
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Mexico's resistance to 'zero appeal' snapback as sovereignty infringement was central conflict R2-R7; ultimate concession in R7 was the breakthrough
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Media actor shaped messaging strategy and headline framing but did not drive substantive positions; amplifier role, not driver
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Room treated protocol amendment as necessary to achieve ratification; original USMCA package explicitly deemed unratifiable without labor enforcement upgrade

node: Node 2 - Domestic Ratification Pressure Room (initial USMCA package formed, before the 10 Dec 2019 Protocol of Amendment; information cutoff 2019-12-09)
